extracted.intended_audience: EPO examiners, patent attorneys, applicants before the EPO
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how and when the description and drawings may be used in examining the clarity (Article 84 EPC) of patent claims, based on EPO boards of appeal case law. Covers limits, exceptions, and examples (parameters, vague terms, self-contradictory claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of description and drawings to interpret claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Boards have interpreted the claims in the light of the description and drawings in order to establish whether they were clear and concise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several decisions (e.g. T 456/91, T 860/93) accept that the description may be used to interpret claims; the case law also notes that a patent may be its own dictionary (see II.A.6.3.3). However, this principle is subject to limits described in subsequent entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth of a term is acceptable if unambiguous to the skilled person
rubrics_metrics.description: The clarity of a claim is not diminished by the mere breadth of a term of art contained in it, if the meaning of such term was unambiguous for a person skilled in the art, either per se or in the light of the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: T 456/91 – although an extremely large number of compounds could be used, it was clear from the claims when read in the light of the description which peptides were suitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must be clear in themselves (no reliance on the description)
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 84 EPC requires that claims must be clear in themselves when read using normal skills, including knowledge of the prior art but not any knowledge derived from the description contained in the patent application or the amended patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities: T 2/80, T 454/89, T 412/03, T 129/13, T 412/02, T 908/04. The requirement means it must be possible to understand the claims without reference to the description; claims should not rely on the description to remove self-contradictions or basic obscurity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art.69 EPC (interpretation for extent of protection) cannot cure Art.84 clarity defects
rubrics_metrics.description: While Art.69 EPC allows the description to be used to interpret the claims for the purpose of determining extent of protection, it is not concerned with a claim's definition of the matter for which protection is sought (Art.84 EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore, in examination or opposition an applicant/patentee cannot rely on Art.69 as a substitute for an amendment necessary to remedy a lack of clarity (T 454/89, T 760/90, T 1129/97, confirmed in T 56/04, T 64/03, T 1265/13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise definition in the description does not automatically make an unclear claim clear
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere fact that the precise meaning of an unclear term is expressly disclosed in the description but not in the claims does not mean that the claims meet the clarity requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority: T 1129/97 (example: 'low alkyl' defined in description does not cure unclear claim wording). See also T 49/99 and T 623/13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity deficiency in claim wording is not rectified by description or drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: A clarity deficiency in the claim wording is not remedied by the fact that the description and drawings would help the reader to understand the technical subject-matter that the claim was intended to define.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority: T 49/99. The claims themselves must define the subject-matter clearly; supporting material cannot be used to fix ambiguous claim language except as limited by case law (see exception entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptional allowance where a vague claim term is defined only in the description
rubrics_metrics.description: A vague or unclear term used in the claim and a precise definition only in the description can be allowed only in exceptional cases if the precise definition cannot be incorporated into the claim and the precise definition is unambiguously and directly identifiable by a skilled person from the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority: T 56/04 (mutatis mutandis reference to R.29(6) EPC 1973). The board emphasised that an exception is narrow: e.g. a specific value disclosed in the description that could instead have been incorporated into the claim will not justify the exception (T 56/04, T 623/13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unclear technical feature prevents identification beyond doubt, especially for delimitation from prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim containing an unclear technical feature prevents its subject-matter from being identified beyond doubt; this is particularly problematic if the unclear feature is meant to delimit the claimed subject-matter from the state of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority: T 56/04. Such lack of clarity undermines the claim's function to delimit the monopoly and therefore usually requires amendment rather than reliance on the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of parameters in claims — need for clarity on how parameters are measured
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a product is characterised by parameters, it must be clear from the claim itself how those parameters are to be determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See II.A.3.5 for detail. However, boards have in some cases justified that the claim need not include the procedure for measuring the parameter (e.g. T 992/02), so whether the measurement method must be in the claim depends on the circumstances and whether the skilled person can determine the parameter unambiguously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-contradictory claims remain unclear despite description
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim does not comply with the clarity requirement if it is not, per se, free of contradiction; it must be possible to understand the claims without reference to the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities: T 2/80 and repeated in T 454/89 and others. If a claim is self-contradictory, the description cannot be used to resolve that contradiction for Art.84 purposes.
